name: Residual-based iterative refinement
definition: Given an approximate solution x to Ax=b, compute r=b−Ax, solve Aδ=r using the existing factorization, then update x←x+δ; repeat subject to residual and iteration limits.
variables: A square matrix; b right side; x approximation; r residual; δ correction
assumptions: Nonsingular A; sufficiently accurate residual computation and correction solve; explicit stopping criteria.
limitations: May stagnate or diverge for ill-conditioned systems or inaccurate solves; mixed precision requires separate assumptions.
failure_conditions: Nonfinite correction, stalled residual or singular factorization
computation: Evaluate residual, solve correction, update, check true residual.

source.citation: Nicholas J. Higham (2023), What Is Iterative Refinement?, basic algorithm and discussion of residual precision. https://nhigham.com/2023/03/13/what-is-iterative-refinement/

application: General numerical linear-system correction on authorised or synthetic matrices.
required_inputs: Matrix, right-hand side, factorization, approximation, tolerances and iteration bound.
incompatible_methods: Assuming refinement guarantees accuracy for every matrix
mechanism_note: Reuses a factorization for residual correction rather than repeating a direct factorization or using Jacobi/Gauss–Seidel coordinate updates. Exact correction would terminate in one step; finite-precision improvement is conditional.

name: Spectral condition number of a nonsingular matrix
definition: For nonsingular real square A, κ₂(A)=||A||₂||A⁻¹||₂=σ_max(A)/σ_min(A).
variables: A square matrix; σ_max and σ_min extreme singular values; κ₂ condition number
assumptions: Nonsingular finite matrix and consistently defined spectral norm; handle singular matrices separately.
limitations: Worst-case sensitivity, not an observed numerical error or a guarantee of actual error magnitude.
failure_conditions: Zero smallest singular value or unreliable singular value estimates
computation: Estimate extreme singular values and their ratio; report singular or unresolved if denominator is zero or uncertain.

source.citation: University of Illinois CS 357, Singular Value Decompositions, 2-Norm Condition Number. https://courses.physics.illinois.edu/cs357/sp2021/notes/ref-16-svd.html

application: General sensitivity diagnostic for a numerical linear system.
required_inputs: Matrix or reliable estimates of its extreme singular values.
incompatible_methods: Confusing a condition bound with measured forward error
mechanism_note: Sensitivity diagnostic derived from extreme singular values, not another SVD algorithm or measured backward error. A certified singular square matrix has infinite condition number.
